evals.prompt: Plan the test strategy for a new tiered-pricing function (quantity discounts at 10 / 50 / 100 units, a percentage cap, rejects negative quantity): what to test, at which levels, and the prioritized cases.
evals.expected_output: A test-strategy artifact: scope (the pricing function), risk areas (the 10/50/100 tier boundaries, negative/zero quantity, rounding, the cap), test levels (unit plus property/boundary, integration where wired), and a prioritized case list (boundaries and error paths first).
assertions: The strategy identifies the real risk areas (tier boundaries, negative/zero input, rounding, the cap)
It spans more than one test level (e.g. unit plus property/boundary), not only a happy-path test
It lists prioritized, concrete cases (boundaries and error paths), not vague advice
It is produced as a test-strategy artifact (type/feature/status with a non-empty test_levels)

evals.prompt: We are about to build a login rate-limiter (5 attempts / 15 min per account, then lockout). Plan the test strategy.
evals.expected_output: A test-strategy covering the limit boundary (5th vs 6th attempt), window expiry, per-account isolation, concurrency/races, and lockout reset — across unit and integration levels, with abuse/security cases prioritized.
assertions: The strategy covers the limit boundary, window expiry, and per-account isolation
It includes concurrency or abuse cases, not just the happy path
It spans unit and integration levels and is produced as a test-strategy artifact

component.purpose: Phase workflow: plan what to test for a change/feature (risk areas, test levels, prioritized cases) into a test-strategy handoff. Delegates to the qa-engineer role; gated at Tier-1 (routing), with test-design quality covered by that role's Tier-2 and the Tier-3 spine.
